'''SWCCG regions''' are named Star Wars planets used as the geographic units of organized play. Each region covers a block of real-world states, provinces, or countries. A Regional Championship for that region has been a Worlds qualifier under both [[Decipher]] and the [[Players Committee]].

== Decipher era ==

Decipher ran Regional Championships as the local step on the road to the World Championship. A 9 February 2002 Game Players Network release, reprinted on TheForce.Net, held up a 1998 Regional road trip as the model the Players Committee was bringing back. It said both finalists of each Regional would receive byes into Day 2 of Worlds.<ref name="tfn-hyperspace">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/The_Hyperspace_Lane_to_the_World_Championships_68998.asp The Hyperspace Lane to the World Championships], TheForce.Net, Josh, 9 February 2002 (Game Players Network release). Archive: [https://web.archive.org/web/20121001051557/http://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/The_Hyperspace_Lane_to_the_World_Championships_68998.asp Wayback, 1 October 2012].</ref>

The same names already appear on the 2000 Worlds invitation list. Trandosite's Countdown to DecipherCon page listed each invitee by the championship that sent them, including one Regional per named planet and two Coruscant championships.<ref name="trando-2000">[https://web.archive.org/web/20011027164817fw_/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/worlds00.htm World Championships 2000 / Countdown to DecipherCon], Trandosite (Wayback, 27 October 2001). Earlier capture: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010810204530/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/worlds00.htm 10 August 2001].</ref> Open and continental seats sat beside the Regionals: Comic Con, Origins, Dragon Con, Wizard World, Australasian Champion, European Champion, North American Champion, and the defending World Champion.

Each planet covered a fixed set of states, provinces, or countries, the same for Star Wars CCG and Young Jedi.<ref name="tfn-regions">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020809145043/http://www.theforce.net/ccg/regions/ TheForce.Net CCG regions index] (Wayback, 9 August 2002; page stamp LAST UPDATED: 10.16.01).</ref> Residence was the rule: a player competed in the Regional of the place they lived; a student could choose school or home, and only one.<ref name="tfn-hyperspace" />

=== Rebel Squadron volunteers (1999–2001) ===

Decipher's volunteer site listed its Rebel Squadron members by tournament region: "more than 200 key volunteers serving Star Wars Customizable Card Game communities around the world".<ref name="decsq-index">[http://www.decipher.com/volunteers/squadrons/index.html Volunteers: Star Wars CCG Squadrons], decipher.com. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000525220411/http://www.decipher.com/volunteers/squadrons/index.html Internet Archive, 25 May 2000]</ref> Squadron members directed sanctioned tournaments and regional qualifiers, ran demos, and helped at conventions.<ref name="decsq-index" /> The index page's featured volunteer was [[Paul Todd Feldman]] (Red 16, Alderaan).<ref name="decsq-index" /> See [[Squadron Members]] for the full squadron rosters.

A 1997 Texas Regional at Texas A&amp;M University in College Station sent its winner to the 64-player Worlds field in Norfolk.<ref name="ars">[https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2015/12/that-one-time-i-played-in-the-star-wars-card-game-world-championship/ That one time I played in the Star Wars card game world championship], Ars Technica, 5 December 2015. Archive: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008210936/https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2015/12/that-one-time-i-played-in-the-star-wars-card-game-world-championship/ Wayback, 8 October 2026].</ref>

== Players Committee ==

Decipher's last Worlds were 2001. The Players Committee reinstated the Regional qualifier path for 2002: up to one championship per named region, open to residents of that region, with 1st and 2nd receiving Day 2 byes at DecipherCon, alongside five summer Opens (Origins, Gen Con, Dragon Con, San Diego Comic-Con, Essen) and Mini-Opens.<ref name="tfn-hyperspace" /><ref name="dgma-2002">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020810221521/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/champcircuit/index.html 2002 Championship Circuit], decipher.com / DGMA (Wayback, 10 August 2002).</ref> Michael Girard signed that GPN release for Player Relations; John Arendt was the contact for volunteering or sponsoring an event.<ref name="tfn-hyperspace" />

Jerry's 15 March 2002 TheForce.Net press release listed the same planet names with tournament directors. It gave the first dated 2002 sites (Alderaan in Modesto, Calamari in Brisbane, Concord Dawn in Paris, Ithor at Libreria SaGa, Yavin 4 in Oxford, North Carolina). Regions still looking for a director then included Coruscant, Kashyyyk, Naboo, Ord Mantell, Tierfon, and Toola.<ref name="tfn-jerry">[https://theforce.net/ccg/story/SWCCG_Regionals_Press_Release_68420.asp SWCCG Regionals Press Release], TheForce.Net, Jerry, 15 March 2002. Archive: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008210220/https://theforce.net/ccg/story/SWCCG_Regionals_Press_Release_68420.asp Wayback, 8 October 2026].</ref> That 2002 list put Turkey in Sullust, Nova Scotia in Hoth: Ice Plains and Yukon in Hoth: North Ridge. It described Outer Rim as unaffiliated areas with a Mexico City director.

[[Tournament Guidelines|Tournament Guide 2.2]] (July 2018) classifies Regional Championships as Level 2 events (with European Nationals). States, Provincials, Districts, and Mini-Opens are Level 1. The Guide requires a State, Regional, Provincial, District, or National to be held in the location named in the title.<ref name="tg22">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Star-Wars-CCG-Tournament-Guide-2.2.pdf Star Wars CCG Official Tournament Guide 2.2] (revised July 2018), section 3.12. Archive: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260928143710/https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Star-Wars-CCG-Tournament-Guide-2.2.pdf Wayback, 28 September 2026].</ref>

The committee kept the planet names, split several of the original Decipher blocks, and retired Outer Rim and the separate Belgian region Tierfon. Current maps and the written coverage list live on the Players Committee forum thread Region Maps, started 3 December 2013 by [[Keith Brown]] (forum handle darkjediknight11, Communications Advocate).<ref name="forum-maps">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=53246 Region Maps], Players Committee forum, first post by darkjediknight11, 3 December 2013.</ref>

County lines printed on that map (and in the forum first post) are:<ref name="forum-maps" />

* '''Pennsylvania:''' Potter, Clinton, Centre, Huntingdon, and Franklin, and everything west of them, are Corellia. Everything east of them is Coruscant.
* '''California:''' San Luis Obispo, Kern, and San Bernardino, and everything south of them, are Scarif. Everything north of them is Alderaan.
* '''Nevada:''' Clark County is Scarif. All other counties are Alderaan.

=== Written coverage on the Region Maps thread ===

The first post of the Region Maps thread (3 December 2013) still prints a written United States and International list under the 2025 pictures. That list already has Bothawui, Nal Hutta, Scarif, Malastare, Kessel, Fondor, Kiffex, Dathomir, and Belgium inside Ryloth.<ref name="forum-maps" /> Robbie Hendon (rhendon) wrote on 6 February 2025 that the text under the photos should be updated or removed to match the new maps.<ref name="rhendon">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=53246 Region Maps], Players Committee forum, rhendon, 6 February 2025.</ref>

A May 2021 reply in the same thread (imrahil327) recorded why Pennsylvania is split: Philadelphia players traveled to New York events, and Pittsburgh players went west.<ref name="imrahil">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=53246 Region Maps], Players Committee forum, imrahil327, May 2021.</ref>

=== Later splits with published Regionals ===

These named regions appear in Players Committee Regional Championship wrap pages after the original Decipher blocks:

{| class="wikitable sortable"
|-
! Region !! First published Regional on the PC results desk !! Notes
|-

|-
| Bothawui || Hastings, Nebraska, 18 June 2022 || Winner Eric Garchow. Nebraska had been inside Decipher Bespin.<ref name="pc-2022">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2022-06-2022-regional-championship-events/ 2022 Regional Championship Events], starwarsccg.org (Bothawui, Hastings, Nebraska, 18 June 2022).</ref>
|-
| Scarif || Burbank, California, 17 November 2024 || Winner Ryan Jellison. Southern California / Arizona split from Alderaan and Tatooine.<ref name="pc-2024">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2024-02-regional-championships/ 2024-02 Regional Championships], starwarsccg.org (Scarif Regionals, Burbank, California, 17 November 2024).</ref>
|}

On 13 August 2022 the committee ran four United States Regionals and a Georgia State Championship (Dagobah) on the same Saturday. The Regionals were Endor in Lynnwood, Washington; Alderaan in Pasadena, California; Bespin in South Saint Paul, Minnesota; and Coruscant in East Norriton, Pennsylvania. The wrap named that weekend #SWCCGSuperSaturday; the accompanying United States graphic is credited to Jared Napolitano and Dan Tartaglione.<ref name="super-sat">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/swccgsupersaturday-wrap-up/ #SWCCGSuperSaturday Wrap-up], starwarsccg.org, 16 August 2022 (events 13 August 2022). Archive: [https://web.archive.org/web/20220818065215/https://www.starwarsccg.org/swccgsupersaturday-wrap-up/ Wayback, 18 August 2022].</ref> Further 2022 Regionals on that schedule included Nal Hutta, Tatooine, Yavin 4, Dagobah, and Corellia.

Recent published Regional sites include Nal Hutta in Indianapolis, Endor in Federal Way, Washington, Yavin 4 in Windsor Mill, Maryland, Bespin in South Saint Paul, Minnesota, Naboo in Liverpool, Corellia in Columbus, Ohio, Coruscant in Long Island City, New York, Tatooine in Denver, and Scarif in Burbank.<ref name="pc-2025">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2025-03-regional-championships/ 2025-03 Regional Championships], starwarsccg.org.</ref><ref name="pc-2026">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2026-05-regional-championships/ 2026-05 Regional Championships], starwarsccg.org.</ref><ref name="pc-2024" />

Forum league boards still use the planet names for local play (SoCal / Scarif League, Nal Hutta League, Dutch/Ryloth League, Tatooine/Denver League, Endor/Seattle League, Dagobah/Atlanta League, and others), including an Outer Rim League board that keeps the retired Decipher region name as a league label.
